styles.name: Swiss Editorial

layout: Use asymmetric columns with aligned edges.
Let one headline establish the entry point.
guidance: Use a clear grid rather than decorative containers.

Honor prefers-reduced-motion and provide immediate feedback.

principles.title: Visual hierarchy
principles.why: Relative emphasis tells people where to begin.
principles.poor: Every heading uses the same weight and size.
principles.improved: Make the task heading dominant; keep metadata quieter but readable.

principles.title: Information architecture
principles.why: Grouping by user intent reduces search effort.
principles.poor: Put billing under a vague Miscellaneous tab.
principles.improved: Group invoices, payment methods, and plans under Billing.

principles.title: Gestalt grouping
principles.poor: Equal gaps inside and between all form sections.
principles.improved: Use smaller gaps inside a group and larger gaps between groups.

principles.title: Typography hierarchy
principles.why: Stable text roles make scanning predictable.
principles.improved: Use body, label, subheading, and heading roles with consistent line heights.

principles.title: Grid and composition
principles.when: Layouts that mix media and text.
principles.poor: Cards and headings drift to unrelated edges.
principles.improved: Align primary regions to a grid that collapses in reading order.

principles.title: Spacing and rhythm
principles.poor: Use arbitrary margins on each item.
principles.improved: Use a small spacing scale and intentional exceptions for emphasis.

principles.title: Color and contrast
principles.why: Color carries meaning only when people can distinguish it.
principles.poor: Use pale gray labels or red alone for errors.
principles.improved: Use sufficient luminance contrast plus an error label and icon when useful.

principles.title: Affordances and feedback
principles.why: People need to know what is actionable and what happened.
principles.poor: Clickable text looks identical to plain text; saving is silent.
principles.improved: Use recognizable controls with focus, pending, success, and error states.

principles.title: Cognitive load
principles.poor: Make users remember IDs across pages.
principles.improved: Keep relevant context visible and show recognition-friendly choices.

principles.title: Progressive disclosure
principles.why: Secondary detail should not block the primary task.
principles.poor: Show every rare option above the main action.
principles.improved: Expose common controls first and label an accessible advanced section.

principles.title: Responsive design
principles.why: Content and tasks must survive changes in available space.
principles.when: Every screen size and zoom level.
principles.poor: Shrink a desktop dashboard into unreadable columns.
principles.improved: Reflow by priority; allow purposeful table scrolling with visible labels.

principles.title: Accessibility
principles.why: Semantic structure and robust interaction widen access.
principles.poor: A div acts as a button and loses keyboard access.
principles.improved: Use a button, visible focus, meaningful label, and appropriate disabled behavior.

principles.title: Interaction states
principles.why: A complete state model prevents ambiguity and dead ends.
principles.poor: Design only a successful populated screen.
principles.improved: Provide empty, loading, error, partial, disabled, and success states.

principles.title: Motion and reduced motion
principles.why: Movement can explain continuity but can also distract or harm.
principles.poor: Looping decorations run beside a reading task.
principles.improved: Use brief purposeful transitions and remove nonessential motion on request.

principles.title: Content-first design
principles.why: Real content exposes structural needs that filler hides.
principles.poor: Design around three identical short placeholder headings.
principles.improved: Use realistic long titles, empty data, errors, and translated text.

principles.title: Consistency versus differentiation
principles.why: Stable interaction patterns let distinctive content remain usable.
principles.poor: Invent a new checkout interaction to appear unique.
principles.improved: Keep checkout familiar and express identity through content and composition.

antiPatterns.title: Generic SaaS composition
antiPatterns.description: Interchangeable hero, logo strip, cards, and CTA regardless of product.
antiPatterns.why: It hides the actual user decision.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: The sequence genuinely answers buyer questions.
antiPatterns.detection: Human review against product goals and content.
antiPatterns.alternative: Lead with task evidence and a product-specific narrative.
antiPatterns.limitation: Composition alone cannot establish poor quality.

antiPatterns.title: Decorative gradient repetition
antiPatterns.description: Many gradients compete without encoding information.
antiPatterns.why: It dilutes hierarchy and may obscure text.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Gradients express a coherent brand or data relationship.
antiPatterns.detection: Static count is a heuristic; inspect the rendered view.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use quieter surfaces and one purposeful emphasis.
antiPatterns.limitation: Source count does not show simultaneous visibility.

antiPatterns.title: Decorative glassmorphism
antiPatterns.description: Translucent panels are used without a layering purpose.
antiPatterns.why: Background variation can damage contrast and focus.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Layering communicates a meaningful spatial relationship.
antiPatterns.detection: Review transparency and backdrop effects in context.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use opaque surfaces or controlled backgrounds.
antiPatterns.limitation: Rendered backgrounds are required for contrast conclusions.

antiPatterns.title: Repetitive feature-card grids
antiPatterns.description: Different information is forced into identical tiles.
antiPatterns.why: Equal weight hides sequence and priority.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Items are genuinely comparable and independent.
antiPatterns.detection: Inspect repeated components and content relationships.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use editorial hierarchy, lists, or comparison tables.
antiPatterns.limitation: Repeated components are not automatically a problem.

antiPatterns.title: Excessive pills
antiPatterns.description: Most surfaces and controls use fully rounded shapes.
antiPatterns.why: Categories and actions become hard to distinguish.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Chips and short related filters benefit from the shape.
antiPatterns.alternative: Assign shapes to roles with a small radius scale.
antiPatterns.limitation: A numeric radius cannot determine appropriateness.

antiPatterns.title: Weak typography hierarchy
antiPatterns.description: Text roles are indistinct or arbitrary.
antiPatterns.why: Scanning becomes slow and meaning is unclear.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Quiet hierarchy suits a simple linear reading task.
antiPatterns.detection: Count declared families and inspect role consistency.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use stable roles with deliberate contrast in scale or weight.
antiPatterns.limitation: Static declarations cannot reveal the actual hierarchy.

antiPatterns.title: Generic hero copy
antiPatterns.description: Claims such as unlock your potential replace concrete value.
antiPatterns.why: Users cannot tell what the product does.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: A campaign line is paired with clear explanatory copy.
antiPatterns.detection: Human review: identify audience, task, outcome, and evidence.
antiPatterns.alternative: Name the user, action, and useful result.
antiPatterns.limitation: No universal phrase list proves copy is poor.

antiPatterns.title: Inconsistent spacing
antiPatterns.description: Unrelated values accumulate without structural meaning.
antiPatterns.why: Groups become ambiguous and maintenance harder.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Optical corrections or content constraints need exceptions.
antiPatterns.detection: Compare declared values to project tokens.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use tokens and record justified exceptions.
antiPatterns.limitation: A hardcoded value may be a deliberate exception.

antiPatterns.title: Arbitrary animation
antiPatterns.description: Movement repeats without explaining state or continuity.
antiPatterns.why: It increases distraction and can delay tasks.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Animation clarifies a transition or rewards an explicit action.
antiPatterns.detection: Review animation purpose and reduced-motion behavior.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use direct feedback with an accessible static alternative.
antiPatterns.limitation: A source-level audit cannot determine perceived distraction.

antiPatterns.title: Visual noise
antiPatterns.description: Too many competing borders, icons, colors, and effects.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Dense signals support an expert monitoring workflow.
antiPatterns.detection: Rendered review with a task-based scan.
antiPatterns.alternative: Remove redundant encodings and group related signals.
antiPatterns.limitation: Expert tools may require high information density.

antiPatterns.title: Poor dashboard density
antiPatterns.description: Tiles consume space while useful comparable data is hidden.
antiPatterns.why: Users travel farther and cannot compare records.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: A small number of summary indicators supports triage.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use tables, trends, units, and purposeful filters.
antiPatterns.limitation: Density is task-dependent, not a maximum-content contest.

antiPatterns.title: Meaningless metrics
antiPatterns.description: Fabricated or context-free numbers imply evidence.
antiPatterns.why: They mislead decisions and erode trust.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Clearly labeled sample data demonstrates a concept.
antiPatterns.detection: Verify provenance, period, denominator, and meaning.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use real sourced metrics or explicitly marked examples.
antiPatterns.limitation: Source syntax cannot establish factual accuracy.

antiPatterns.title: Inappropriate icons
antiPatterns.description: Unfamiliar or decorative icons replace clear labels.
antiPatterns.why: Meaning becomes guesswork, especially across cultures.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: Familiar icons accompany text or labeled controls.
antiPatterns.detection: Review accessible names and user recognition.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use descriptive labels and consistent icon semantics.

antiPatterns.title: Weak responsive behavior
antiPatterns.description: Fixed layouts clip tasks or hide essential controls.
antiPatterns.why: Small screens and zoomed views become unusable.
antiPatterns.acceptableWhen: A data table needs controlled horizontal scrolling.
antiPatterns.detection: Inspect actual narrow viewports, zoom, and long translations.
antiPatterns.alternative: Reflow content priorities and preserve task access.
antiPatterns.limitation: Breakpoints in source do not prove responsive quality.
